EDS AI Workflow (Eitri Agentic Dev Workflow)

Skills catalogue

This catalogue lists every skill in the EDS AI Workflow (Eitri) and the Matt Pocock base set it builds on: what each does, who maintains it, whether it is available, and the arguments it takes. Use it as a reference while working through the other pages.

If you are unsure which skill to run, run /ask-workflow, which asks questions to find the right skill or path across the PO/BA and developer harnesses. For Matt Pocock’s skills alone, run /ask-matt.

Read the conventions

  • Arguments and subcommands have no dashes, such as im8 or [project-root]. They name the target, path or mode.
  • Flags and options start with dashes, such as --kblog or --id. They switch behaviour on or pass named values.
  • Maintained by names the author given in the harness documentation. “CoreX EDS team” marks EDS add-on skills.
  • Status is Available or Planned. Planned skills are in development; do not rely on them as a gate.

Source: [1] introduction.

Setup and metrics

Setup and metrics skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/setup-token-loggingCoreX EDS teamAvailableLogs token usage and cost every time a skill runs. Installs a post-run hook, adds a script for cost reports and updates .gitignore to keep logs local.

Planning

Planning skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/dependency-orchestratorCoreX EDS teamAvailableBreaks user stories into a scheduled dependency graph and generates planning reports: timeline and resourcing estimates for project managers, and an implementation schedule for developers. Supports multi-release planning and add-on stories, up to 200 stories. Step 2.
/stories-to-issuesCoreX EDS teamAvailableReads the orchestrator’s schedule and creates detailed GitHub issues in scheduling order, with acceptance criteria, development tasks, standards references and scheduling metadata.
/reconcile-storiesCoreX EDS teamAvailableUpdates the schedule from actual issue closure times, recomputes remaining work and regenerates the PM and developer reports without changing the original plan structure.

Matt Pocock’s skills

These base skills are installed unchanged from Matt Pocock’s public skill set. Notes describe how this workflow uses them.

Matt Pocock’s skills used in the workflow
SkillStatusWhat it does
/ask-mattAvailableAn interactive guide to Matt Pocock’s engineering skills, from idea to shipping, including bug diagnosis and codebase health.
/setup-matt-pocock-skillsAvailableConfigures the repository’s issue tracker, triage labels and domain-document layout. Run once, before /dependency-orchestrator (Step 1).
/wayfinderAvailablePlans work too large for one agent session as a shared map of investigation tickets, resolved one at a time. For existing codebases, ask it to cross-reference the plan against the code so legacy constraints are not missed. Path 2 and Step 5.
/grill-with-docsAvailableStress-tests a plan for a well-defined story against the domain model and saves the agreed context to CONTEXT.md and ADRs. Step 5. Used in the workflow steps but not listed in the harness skills catalogue.
/grill-meAvailableQuestions you about an artefact until it matches your intent. Optional after any planning artefact, and at HITL 1 and HITL 2. Used in the workflow steps but not listed in the harness skills catalogue.
/grillingAvailableQuestions you relentlessly about a plan or design before building. Called by /wayfinder for grilling tickets.
/domain-modelingAvailableBuilds and sharpens the project’s domain model and ubiquitous language, and records architectural decisions. Called by /wayfinder.
/codebase-designAvailableShared vocabulary for designing deep modules: interfaces, seams, testability and AI navigability. Pair it with /wayfinder during domain alignment.
/prototypeAvailableBuilds a throwaway prototype to answer a design question about a state model, logic or what a UI should look like.
/to-specAvailableTurns the current conversation into a specification and publishes it to the tracker, without further questions. Produces the TRD in Step 6.
/to-ticketsAvailableBreaks a plan or specification into tracer-bullet tickets with declared blocking edges and publishes them to the tracker. Step 9.
/improve-codebase-architectureAvailableScans for deepening opportunities, presents them in an HTML report, then questions you through the one you pick. Step 13.
/code-reviewAvailableReviews changes since a fixed point along two axes in parallel sub-agents: repository coding standards, and the originating issue or PRD. Step 15 and inside Gate 2.
/diagnosing-bugsAvailableA diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Step 16.

Frontend quality

The Impeccable suite by Paul Bakaus covers frontend quality in three layers. Install it once with npx impeccable skills install.

Impeccable frontend quality commands
CommandWhen to useWhat it covers
/impeccable auditAfter implementing a UI sliceAccessibility (contrast, ARIA, keyboard navigation), performance (layout thrashing, re-renders), theming (hard-coded colours, dark mode), responsive design (touch targets, overflow) and generated-code anti-patterns.
/impeccable hardenBefore shipping a featureResilience: edge cases, error and empty states, text overflow in other languages and slow networks.
/impeccable polishOn prototypes or before a stakeholder reviewVisual finish: alignment, typography, spacing, interaction states and copy.

Compliance

Compliance skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/policiesCoreX EDS teamAvailableLoads the organisational policy references and applies them to audit a document for security and governance compliance.
/spec-complianceCoreX EDS teamAvailableVets a specification or TRD against the policy references. Step 8.
/issue-verificationCoreX EDS teamAvailableVets issues from /to-tickets or /stories-to-issues to confirm each is a true tracer bullet and the set is consistent, before publishing. Step 10.

Policy references ship with the policies skill: IM8 security controls (36 controls) and the ARC agentic AI governance framework (88 controls). Read how to add your own.

Implementation

/do-work adapts Matt Pocock’s /implement with a compliance gate wired into its feedback loop. /code-reviewer is the review dispatcher embedded in that loop.

Implementation skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/do-workCoreX EDS team, adapted from Matt Pocock’s /implementAvailableExecutes a unit of work end to end: implement, review, validate with type checks and tests, then commit. Flag: --kblog. Step 12.
/code-reviewerCoreX EDS teamAvailableRuns the registered quality and compliance reviews in parallel against recent changes and writes artifacts/code-reviewer/{slug}-compliance.html. Called by the /do-work gate and the pre-commit hook, or run manually.
/mutation-testingCoreX EDS team, wrapping PIT, Stryker, mutmut and Cosmic RayAvailableFinds surviving mutations, weak assertions and missing coverage, detecting the project’s tool automatically. Run on changed files after the loop is clean; full runs belong in nightly CI. Gate 3.
/git-commit-skillCoreX EDS teamAvailableCreates Conventional Commits, splitting changes into one logical change each.
/browser-testCoreX EDS team, wrapping agent-browser by VercelAvailableBuilds and runs the application and executes acceptance scenarios from the issue in a live browser, with screenshot evidence. Step 17.
/e2eCoreX EDS teamAvailableSets up a Playwright story end-to-end harness and turns user stories into repeatable browser tests with fresh Allure evidence. Subcommand stability repeats a campaign’s frozen scenarios to detect results that change between runs. Step 19.
/html-to-shadcnCoreX EDS teamPlannedWill convert a PO/BA HTML prototype into a Shadcn component scaffold in src/components/features/<screen-name>/, ready for the developer to wire up. Step 11.

Review

/code-reviewer dispatches these reviewers in parallel. Each can also be run on its own.

Review skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/build-checkCoreX EDS teamAvailableBuild checks for changed TypeScript, React and Java code: formatting, type checking or compilation, tests, coverage thresholds, production builds and codebase audits. Gate 1.
/im8-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableChecks IM8 application technical controls against a React with TypeScript and Spring Boot codebase, automating what it can and flagging manual review items.
/semgrepCoreX EDS team, wrapping SemgrepAvailableStatic analysis of changed code for vulnerabilities, hard-coded secrets, injection, insecure deserialisation and unsafe patterns.
/thermo-nuclear-reviewCursorAvailableA very strict maintainability review of abstraction quality, oversized files and growing conditional complexity.
/react-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews React code for bugs, style issues and best practices.
/spring-core-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews Spring applications for bugs, style issues and best practices.
/spring-web-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews Spring Web MVC code: REST APIs, routing, validation, exception handling and testing.
/spring-data-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews Spring Data JPA: entity mapping, query performance, transactions and persistence practices.
/spring-security-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews Spring Security configuration: filter chains, method security, OIDC and OAuth2, sessions, CSRF and CORS, response headers, and that development bypasses and seeded data are confined to development profiles.
/spring-logging-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews logging: SLF4J use, levels, exception logging, sensitive and personal data leakage, log injection, MDC and correlation IDs, and structured output. Also the observability gate at pre-production.
/spring-test-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews Spring Boot tests: test slices, Testcontainers integration tests, mock beans and context caching, and web and data-layer tests.
/spring-batch-reviewCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews Spring Batch jobs, bulk data processing and offline tasks.
/spec-standards-checkCoreX EDS teamAvailableChecks a specification against the standards and questions referenced on its issue, flagging critical gaps and warnings. Step 7.
/sonar-reviewCoreX EDS teamPlannedWill audit changed files against the team’s Sonar quality profiles and architecture constraints through the Sonar MCP integration, enforcing what the CI Sonar gate would block on.

Architecture linting

These skills turn architecture decisions into runnable boundary tests, so violations fail the build. They assume a JVM backend with ArchUnit, a JavaScript or TypeScript frontend with dependency-cruiser, or both. Run the plan and generate skills once during setup, and the feature skill after each feature.

Architecture linting skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/arch-tests-planCoreX EDS teamAvailableAnalyses the project and writes arch/arch-test-plan.md: the architecture style, standard and ADR-derived rules, and a test row for each. Step 4.
/arch-tests-genCoreX EDS team, wrapping ArchUnit and dependency-cruiserAvailableGenerates ArchUnit tests and dependency-cruiser configuration from the plan. Step 4.
/arch-tests-gen-featureCoreX EDS team, wrapping ArchUnit and dependency-cruiserAvailableGenerates tests for one feature by filling the plan’s Feature Template rows with its real package or folder names. Step 14.

Path to production

These skills run before a release is promoted. /pre-prod-check runs them all in sequence; each can also be run alone. See when each runs.

Path to production skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does

/gen-code-docsCoreX EDS teamAvailableGenerates HTML API documentation from TSDoc and Javadoc comments. Argument: [project-root].
/gen-auth-matrixCoreX EDS teamAvailableGenerates an authorisation matrix to verify access controls and permissions across roles.

Additional skills

These skills sit outside the numbered steps. Use them as needed during design and review.

Additional skills
SkillMaintained byStatusWhat it does
/ask-workflowCoreX EDS teamAvailableAn interactive guide that asks questions to find the skill or path that fits your situation, from requirements to development.
/backwards-mappingCoreX EDS teamAvailableTraces requirements from business value to entry points through first-principles dependency mapping, to find vertical slices and protect security and architecture. Use it for new systems or complex features.
/fry-meCoreX EDS team, adapted from Matt PocockAvailableQuestions you relentlessly about a plan or decisions until you reach a shared understanding. Called by /issue-verification.
/owasp-threat-modelingCoreX EDS team, wrapping OWASP Threat DragonAvailableProduces a threat model with data-flow diagrams, STRIDE or LINDDUN threats and a findings report. Use it when designing a feature or preparing a security design review.
/pragmatic-reviewerCoreX EDS teamAvailableReviews a design, proposal or strategy using inversion and second-order thinking, separating must-fix flaws from acceptable trade-offs.
/query-kbCoreX EDS teamAvailableQueries an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base, for a user or for another skill. Flags: --id KB_ID, --tag KEY=VALUE.
/update-standardsCoreX EDS teamPlannedWill review standards documents against current best practice and technology versions, finding breaking changes, deprecations, new patterns and contradictions between documents. It will question you on each finding, apply only approved changes and keep an audit trail.

Next step: run /ask-workflow in your repository and compare its suggestion with the step you expected. Then return to the overview to see where that step sits.
